newsitem.title: USA: White House to release fundraising documents.
newsitem.headline: White House to release fundraising documents.

text.p: The White House on Tuesday prepared to release documents showing President Bill Clinton was "enthusiastic" about having friends and supporters stay at the White House but denied the invitations were an inducement for campaign donations.

Presidential spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters that the documents, which belong to former top aide Harold Ickes, do show Clinton was "determined to do all he could" to redress the Democratic Party's defeat in the 1994 congressional elections. But he also insisted that use of the White House Lincoln Bedroom for special guests was not a reward for campaign money.

McCurry said the documents, to be released around midday, concern "the way in which the 1996 (campaign) fundraising effort was structured." He said they "reflect a president very determined to do all he could in the aftermath of the 1994 defeat to organize the party and to organize his own efforts towards the political challenges we faced in 1996."
McCurry said the documents would list people whom Clinton invited to stay in the Lincoln Bedroom at the White House, but said that those asked were mostly friends and backers.

"The president was enthusiastic about having friends and supporters to the Lincoln Bedroom," McCurry said. "You'll see later today when you see the names of those who stayed at the Lincoln Bedroom ... they are largely friends and supporters."

Asked if there was any "quid pro quo" between the stays at the White House and campaign donations, he replied: "No ... I've always said that among the people that he entertained at the White House were people who were supporters."
